title: The integers embed in a field of characteristic zero; $\Ql$ and its extensions have characteristic zero
statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, that is, $n\cdot1_K
eq0$ for every integer $n
eq0$. Then the unique ring homomorphism $\mathbf Z	o K$, $c\mapsto c\cdot1_K$, is injective. For every prime $\ell$, the field $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ of $\ell$-adic numbers has characteristic zero, and so has every field $L$ containing $\Ql$ as a subfield (for instance an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$): $n\cdot1_L$ is the image of $n\cdot1_{\Ql}
eq0$ under the injective inclusion. Hence $\mathbf Z	o\Ql$ and $\mathbf Z	o L$ are injective.
